# Module 3: Quoting, estimating and proposals

*A priced quote on your own rates in minutes, from site or the office.*

**Who does it in a small business:** Owner or estimator, admin types it up.

## The typical process

Every business does it a bit differently. This is the common shape we see.

| # | Step | What happens | Tools | Where time goes |
|:-:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Request comes in | Email, plans, a site visit, photos | Outlook, Gmail, PDF |  |
| 2 | Check it's enough | Chase anything missing before pricing | Outlook, Phone | slow |
| 3 | Measure or take off | On site or from drawings (module 4) | Paper, PDF, Bluebeam |  |
| 4 | Price it | Rates, materials, supplier prices, labour | Excel, Supplier email | slow |
| 5 | Write the quote | Typed into a template or the job system | Word, ServiceM8, simPRO, Xero | copy-paste |
| 6 | Send and log it | PDF out, logged with a reminder | Outlook, HubSpot | copy-paste |

## Where the time goes

From businesses APG has audited, anonymised. Hours are staff estimates, not measurements.

- 6 in 10 enquiries go back for missing information before they can be priced
- Matching products takes 1 to 2 h on a complex quote; the whole quote 3 to 4 h
- The same job written out three times: site notes, Excel, then Word
- Rebuilding quotes after site visits: about 13 h a week across one team

## Step 1: the intake

`/quote-intake`: Walk through your last two quotes: where each number came from, and every step you did by hand.

It hands back your own version of the map above, with your tools and your hours, then suggests which skill to build first.

## The skills

- **Quote builder** (connected): Voice note and photos in, a quote on your prices out. Built and live for clients
- **Missing-info check** (connected): Reads the enquiry and drafts the questions before you price
- **Sheet to skill** (drop in a file): Drop in the spreadsheet you quote from; it becomes the plugin's questions
